governingDocuments.AGENTS.md: The repository owner's standing branch policy and agent rules (also linked from CLAUDE.md) - read this before acting on anything in this file. Covers: development is the only branch to push to without explicit permission; main is only touched on explicit owner instruction, and only via the release branch + promote-release.yml, never a direct push; PR #11 (ci-monitor -> main) must never be merged or closed, backed by block-pr-7.yml's check and guard-ci-monitor-pr.yml's auto-reopen; the AI-to-AI handoff protocol requiring this file and DEVLOG.md to be updated together in every project commit; and the standing rule against invisible self-repair.
governingDocuments.DEVLOG.md: The chronological, per-commit development log. Its 'Shared AI handoff' section at the top is the human-readable counterpart to this file's structured plan - read it first, every time, per AGENTS.md's 'Read DEVLOG.md first, always' rule. This file (AI-HANDOFF.json) and DEVLOG.md must be updated together in the same commit; neither supersedes the other.
governingDocuments.AI-CONFLICTS.json: The auditable ledger of AI-agent conflicts (concurrent or contradictory work between agents), governed by templates/ai-conflict-resolution.md and enforced by .github/workflows/ai-conflict-governance.yml. Never delete, bypass, or disable it.
governingDocuments.CLAUDE.md: Claude-specific entry point; it just points to AGENTS.md, which applies to every AI agent working here, not only Claude.
governingDocuments.README.md: The project's own generated/maintained documentation of what The Crucible does, its CLI, and its workflow steps - kept in sync with source via npm run docs:sync/docs:check.
governingDocuments.templates/ai-conflict-resolution.md: The actual conflict-resolution procedure AGENTS.md and AI-CONFLICTS.json point to: freeze the contested mutation, preserve both sides in the shared handoff, and get an explicit owner decision instead of silently picking a side.
governingDocuments.templates/required-check-rollout.md: The rollout plan AGENTS.md requires for any new required workflow check: report-only on development first, then explicit owner promotion, then npm run audit:required-check, before it is ever added to branch protection or a ruleset. Directly relevant to how `block` must be added as a required check on main.
governingDocuments.templates/agent-boundaries.md: The AI-agent rules for this repository's one-way link to adopter projects that pin The Crucible as a security gate - what an agent may and may not do when investigating a Crucible-related CI failure in a project that consumes this repository.

sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session, no matter which agent or tool is running it, and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt below - even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation. Branch policy, PR locks (e.g. PR #11), and handoff state can all change while an agent is idle; a long gap is treated the same as a fresh session. See AGENTS.md's 'Recheck governingDocuments at the start of every session' rule.
